chunks: Mas‘adah ibn Ṣadaqah has related from al-Imām Ja‘far ibn Muḥammad aṣ-Ṣādiq (a.s.) saying:

Amīr al-mu’minin (a.s.) delivered this sermon from the pulpit of Kūfah, and this was because a man came to him and said to him: ‘O Amīr al-mu’minin! describe our Lord for us as we see Him with our eyes, so that our love for Him may increase and our knowledge of Him may grow.’ He (a.s.) became angry and called out: ‘Salat is gathering!’ (Prayer is to be held in congregation), and the people gathered until the mosque was crowded with its people. Then he ascended the pulpit while he was angry and his color had changed. He praised God Almighty and sent blessings upon the Prophet (s.a.w.s.), then he said:

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ جَامِعَةٌ: Prayer is gathering (call for congregational prayer)

ai.seo_question: What was the specific request made to Imam Ali regarding the description of God in this sermon?
ai.summary: This incident, recorded by Mas'ada ibn Sadaqa, underscores the Shia theological principle of *tanzih* (divine transcendence) by contrasting visual perception with intellectual understanding. Imam Ali’s (a.s.) anger highlights the danger of anthropomorphism (*tashbih*), as the man sought to limit the Infinite by making Him an object of sight, whereas true knowledge comes from recognizing His attributes rather than His essence. This sermon serves as a foundational text for understanding how divine unity is preserved against the human tendency to visualize the Creator.
